archetypes.name: kv-relay
archetypes.rationale: Each new wrapper script must relay its child's stdout KV lines unchanged; a missed or mangled key silently breaks orchestrator routing, which static correctness reviewers are unlikely to catch without the full KV grammar context.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every new wrapper script in `skills/implement/scripts/` for stdout KV relay completeness. For each wrapper, verify that all load-bearing keys named in the plan (e.g. `OOS_CHECKPOINT_RC`, `EMIT_BODY`, `WFR_RC`, `STEP17_EMITTED_PRESENT`, `STALL_TRACKING_*`, routing-envelope keys) are either emitted directly or relayed from the child script's stdout without suppression. Check that each wrapper's exit-code passthrough matches the contract described in the plan — pay special attention to `step-8-oos-checkpoint.sh` (exit-1 vs exit-2 vs other-rc selection) and `step-8-ship.sh` (Python 3.11-guard must emit structured JSON and exit 4 on failure). Verify that `set +e`/`set -e` brackets around child invocations do not accidentally swallow child stdout before it is relayed. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: bash32-compat
archetypes.rationale: Thirteen new wrapper scripts must be Bash 3.2-portable per BASH_AUTHORING.md; violations are non-obvious and CI runs on ubuntu-latest (bash 4+) so regressions only surface on macOS or the lint-bash32 target.
archetypes.prompt_body: Scan every new `.sh` file added in this diff (all 13 wrappers plus `scripts/test-implement-fence-shape.sh`) for Bash 4+ constructs forbidden by BASH_AUTHORING.md §3: associative arrays (`declare -A`), namerefs (`declare -n`, `local -n`), `mapfile`/`readarray`, parameter case conversion (`${var^^}` etc.), append-all redirection (`&>>`), and coprocs. Also check the `rebase-checkpoint-probe.sh` changes: the `BASE_ARGS=()` array-guard (`${BASE_ARGS[@]+…}`) is removed in this diff — confirm no replacement introduces an empty-array nounset hazard on bash 3.2 (`rebase_args+=()` appends are safe, but verify the new `if`-blocks building `rebase_args` handle the zero-element case correctly under `set -u`). Look for any renderer substitution using `${var//pattern/$replacement}` where `$replacement` could contain `&`. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
